answer: A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The onyx multiplier is published, charged in tundra, and walnut lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1687 identities would post 2643 proofs and burn roughly 39 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
